doc: A bisect's predicate is a command the hub does not trust (the project's own test, run over states an agent may have written), so each run is a sealed job: an agent's sandbox, the slot's tree its only writable folder.  Three commits; the third breaks `state`; the predicate also tries to write a file outside its slot, and fails to; the bisect still names the third commit.

args: mkdir -p $ROOT/proj && cd $ROOT/proj && git init -q && echo ok > state && git add state && git -c user.name=t -c user.email=t@t commit -q -m good && echo more > other && git add other && git -c user.name=t -c user.email=t@t commit -q -m 'another file' && echo broken > state && git -c user.name=t -c user.email=t@t commit -qam 'break the state'

argv: cd $ROOT/proj && echo GOOD $(git rev-parse HEAD~2) && exec sleep 300
